1162.skill_name: Verifying core Symptom improvement in mood, Anxiety, etc.
1162.skill_description: Before the ending decision, explicitly ask and summarize the client's current levels and change trajectories of mood, Anxiety, and sustained negative emotions, confirming whether these core symptoms have substantively improved through treatment.
1162.when_to_use: At the assessment and consolidation-goal discussion of the closing stage, used to judge whether the conditions for termination are met.
1162.trigger: The client says 'I feel much better', self-reported Anxiety decreasing or emotions more stable, or actively proposing reducing frequency/ending.

1163.skill_name: Compare symptom improvement with broader changes
1163.skill_description: When symptoms have eased, check whether deeper changes in self-awareness, interpersonal functioning, and adaptability have occurred at the same time; avoid hastily terminating solely on the basis of symptom improvement.
1163.when_to_use: In decision discussions where the client proposes ending because symptoms have eased, or treatment approaches termination.
1163.trigger: The client emphasizes 'once symptoms improve it is almost enough', attributing progress only to reduced discomfort, or avoiding deeper topics.

1164.skill_name: Identifying and normalizing Regression symptoms in the termination phase
1164.skill_description: In the ending stage, anticipate and recognize the brief return of old symptoms or relationship patterns, treating them as phase Regression rather than negating all progress, preventing the termination preparation from being overturned by misreading.
1164.when_to_use: In the termination-phase Listening and assessment, when old symptoms or old relationship reactions appear, used to correctly interpret the client's state and ending readiness.
1164.trigger: The client's old symptoms briefly recur, lateness recurs, entanglement over bills / cancellation policy resumes, or sudden anger and suspicion toward the therapist's concern appears.

1165.skill_name: Discuss possible return of old patterns and review options
1165.skill_description: Convey to the client the reality that 'old ways' may briefly return under future pressure, and explain that short-term follow-up visits can consolidate and correct when needed, supporting maintenance and relapse prevention.
1165.when_to_use: In the summary and goodbye stage of the last few sessions, used to consolidate gains and plan the future.
1165.trigger: The client expresses worries about maintaining in the future, asks about post-ending support, or feels uneasy about having no one listening after goodbye.

1172.skill_description: Guide the client to review changes and explain their causes, observing whether they see the benefits as results of their own abilities and choices rather than 'treatment just happened' or originating from the therapist, to judge whether independence has increased and whether the time to end is approaching.
1172.when_to_use: In the goal consolidation and evaluation of the ending stage, when discussing whether to terminate or formulate a closing plan; the client is overall stable and willing to review the gains of treatment.
1172.trigger: The client attributes change mainly to the treatment or therapist; talks little about their own efforts when discussing progress, or expresses uncertainty about 'without treatment it cannot be maintained'.

1173.skill_name: Identifying and exploring the 'losing gains without treatment' Fantasy
1173.skill_description: Ask the client directly for their view on whether the gains will vanish after they stop treatment, clarify the underlying worry about dependence and separation, and assess the degree of psychological dependence on the therapist's presence and their readiness for ending.
1173.when_to_use: When assessing Independence and discussing termination arrangements in the ending stage, especially facing fragile or highly dependent clients, needing to identify the impact of dependency Fantasies on decisions.
1173.trigger: The client expresses worries about regressing after stopping or 'needing the therapist present' to maintain change; showing strong hesitation and unease about termination.

1174.skill_name: Taper or space sessions to test maintenance capacity
1174.skill_description: According to closing needs, gradually widen session intervals or arrange planned intermissions, observing whether the client's symptoms, emotions, and functioning stay stable with less support, empirically assessing whether improvements can be maintained without ongoing treatment support.
1174.when_to_use: When the client has improved but still worries about termination, or the therapist needs to verify their ability to maintain gains independently; when formulating the transition and termination plan in the ending stage.
1174.trigger: The client wavers between 'ending/continuing', or expresses unease about stopping completely; the therapist worries they still need stable support to maintain functioning.

1209.skill_name: Clarifying open follow-up and re-examination channels
1209.skill_description: Clearly convey to the client that 'the door is open', explaining that in the future, when feeling stressed or excited, they can return for short-term 'check-ins', arranging several booster sessions when necessary, ensuring an accessible support path after termination.
1209.when_to_use: The ending stage approaches or it is the last few interviews; termination by both parties or one party is imminent, requiring consolidation of the gains and handover of the support methods after termination.
1209.trigger: The client asks whether they can still meet after termination, worried about having no one to turn to, or unilaterally proposes termination yet still shows unease and attachment ambivalence.

1210.skill_name: Previewing that future pressure and old patterns may return
1210.skill_description: In the closing dialogue, realistically point out that stress situations will still appear in the future and 'old ways' may resurge, normalizing their predictability, connecting them with the understanding and change already gained, and proposing follow-up calibration when needed.
1210.when_to_use: Before the ending-stage summary and goodbyes; when the client reviews change and discusses future arrangements, needing to consolidate gains and transition to self-management.
1210.trigger: The client expresses ambivalence and Loneliness about parting (e.g. related dreams), worried about future coping or Anxiety and questions about 'old problems returning'.

1211.skill_name: Arranges post-termination medical or regular follow-up (when applicable)
1211.skill_description: For those who need medication management, make clear that even after formal termination, medical examinations can still be conducted monthly; at the same time explain the channels and choices of frequency for follow-up visits, ensuring that necessary safety monitoring and support are maintained beyond termination.
1211.when_to_use: The client is on medication and needs continuous medical management; or clinical assessment deems that minimum fixed monitoring and support are still needed after termination.
1211.trigger: The client is in medication treatment, worried about physiological or medication problems, or proactively proposes hoping for fixed checks and follow-up arrangements.

1166.skill_name: Guiding review and marking specific changes
1166.skill_description: In the ending stage, moderately relax neutrality, actively guide the client to review treatment, point out views or coping different from the past, and jointly sort out how these changes formed, to consolidate and assess self-awareness and adaptive improvement.
1166.when_to_use: At the consolidation and evaluation period of the ending stage, the alliance is solid and nearing termination, needing to summarize changes and examine self-functioning.
1166.trigger: The client self-reports coping in recent social or conflict situations clearly different from before, or says 'I think change happened here'.

1167.skill_name: Connecting emotions and dreams with termination and Directed association
1167.skill_description: For emotions, dreams, or metaphors appearing in the termination period, first require association to confirm their meaning, then clearly connect them with the ending, to examine reflective ability and reality testing, and prioritize understanding the material through the 'lens of ending'.
1167.when_to_use: When new emotions, dreams, or metaphors appear in the ending stage, needing to assess the client's self-reflection and Reflection ability.
1167.trigger: The client reports feelings of 'like falling off a cliff', or narrates dreams and associations about parting, being alone and other themes.

1168.skill_name: Inquire about feelings of moving forward alone to assess independence
1168.skill_description: By naming and exploring the excitement and Anxiety about 'moving forward alone after leaving treatment', connecting it with termination, assessing their handling of dependence and autonomy, to judge readiness for Independence and self-bearing of change.
1168.when_to_use: When termination is imminent, the client talks about post-ending life, plans, or worries and expectations about Being alone.
1168.trigger: The client dreams of undertaking journeys alone (e.g. going to Mars alone) showing coexisting excitement and Anxiety, or expresses wanting to 'try on their own'.

1169.skill_name: Assessing work and recreation functioning and grounding Anticipations
1169.skill_description: In the last few sessions, summarize functional changes in Work, relationships, and recreation, point out representative progress, and propose realistic Anticipations of possible future pressure and old-pattern resurgence, to consolidate functional improvement and self-efficacy.
1169.when_to_use: In the summary and goodbye stage of the last one or two sessions, when sincerely evaluating change and planning the future.
1169.trigger: The client reviews improvements in Work, interpersonal, or social scenes, or asks the therapist's views on overall effectiveness and future challenges.

1170.skill_name: Feed back realistic evaluations of self-awareness and talent limitations
1170.skill_description: Combined with the treatment course, clearly feed back the improvement in the client's self-awareness and their more stable, realistic evaluation of their own talents/limitations, reinforcing self-trust and congruence, as a sign of mature termination and improved ego functioning.
1170.when_to_use: At termination, during 'honest evaluation of change' and 'exchanging views on treatment', used to consolidate self-functioning indicators.
1170.trigger: The client expresses a new understanding of the self, reduced idealization or devaluation, or proactively seeks the therapist's overall feedback on their change.

1171.skill_name: Assess defense adaptation and flexibility by exploring regression
1171.skill_description: Anticipate termination-phase Regression and old symptom/transference reappearance, first treating them as phase characteristics and exploring the Fantasies and emotions behind them, thereby assessing whether they can regulate with more adaptive and flexible defenses and Reflection.
1171.when_to_use: When old-pattern resurgence such as lateness, disputing rules, anger, or jealousy appears in the ending stage, used for functional assessment rather than hastily negating termination.
1171.trigger: The client re-questions the therapist's caring, jealousy or anger toward others escalates, or the early rule disputes and avoidance behaviors reappear.

1197.skill_name: Inviting expression and exploration of final-session Fantasies
1197.skill_description: Before termination, actively ask the client about thoughts and Fantasies regarding the final session (e.g. hugging, avoiding contact), encouraging them to voice wishes and worries, clarifying their meaning through dialogue, valuing expression itself over satisfying the behavior.
1197.when_to_use: In the last few sessions of the ending stage, starting to jointly design the final session, needing to clarify both parties' expectations and arrangements for goodbyes.
1197.trigger: The client mentions 'the last time' 'termination', asks whether to hug or expresses fear of hugging, showing hesitation or tension about goodbye arrangements.

1198.skill_name: Completing goodbyes with a handshake and holding boundaries
1198.skill_description: Clearly and firmly maintain professional boundaries, completing goodbyes with only a handshake at the door; not actively initiating any other physical contact, while acknowledging the handshake's symbolic meaning and emotional weight for the client.
1198.when_to_use: At the ending moment of the final session, when entering the goodbye ritual and needing to implement specific etiquette and boundaries.
1198.trigger: The client proposes hugging or attempts physical contact, or the therapist feels an inner urge to hug; the client gazes or extends a hand hinting at goodbye styles.

1199.skill_name: Gracefully accepting and responding to goodbye gifts
1199.skill_description: If the client brings a gift at the start of the final session, open it in person and invite them to say a few words; do not Interpretation or analyze at this moment, only sincerely thank them, to accept their genuine emotional expression.
1199.when_to_use: When gift exchange appears in the ending session, the moment needing to handle goodbye etiquette and emotional expression.
1199.trigger: The client hands over a gift or says 'a little something for you' or 'a keepsake for you', appearing nervous and expectant of the therapist's reaction.

1200.skill_name: Appropriately responding to personal Questioning while protecting anonymity
1200.skill_description: At termination, answers to factual, low-self-disclosure questions (such as whereabouts, post) may be a little more frequent than earlier, answered concisely to show reciprocity and authenticity, while protecting privacy and anonymity and avoiding crossing boundaries.
1200.when_to_use: In the ending stage the alliance is stable, the client asks about the therapist's whereabouts or real-life information, and moderate reciprocity is needed to support the transition.
1200.trigger: The client asks concrete questions such as 'where will you work next', 'what will you do after the training ends', or 'how can I still contact you'.

1201.skill_name: Conveying closing feedback and genuine affirmation
1201.skill_description: In the last few sessions, briefly review the client's changes and functional improvement with concise statements, ground possible future challenges, express trust and positive feelings, and offer goodbyes and wishes within Good boundaries.
1201.when_to_use: In the summary stage before termination, when the client has reviewed his own changes or expects the therapist's overall view of the treatment.
1201.trigger: The client requests evaluation of treatment effectiveness, talks about self-change and uncertainty, or shows parting emotions and seeks the therapist's response.

1202.skill_name: Normalize fluctuations and explain follow-up options
1202.skill_description: Clearly state that old patterns may resurge under future pressure, normalizing short-term fluctuation; explain that short-term check-ins or a few more sessions can 'get back on track', conveying that 'the door is always open', supporting autonomy without reinforcing dependence.
1202.when_to_use: When formulating post-ending plans, the client worries about relapse or feels uneasy about separation, needing transitional Safety.
1202.trigger: The client expresses worries and questions like 'afraid of returning to the past later' 'can I still come if something happens' 'can I manage on my own'.

1203.skill_name: Supportively avoid forced expression and gradually reduce frequency
1203.skill_description: For clients for whom parting is hard to bear, do not force them to face loss directly; focus mainly on empathizing their gains and continued caring, using gradual frequency reduction or intermittent sessions when necessary, helping them transition smoothly to termination.
1203.when_to_use: In the closing stage, in situations where the client has low tolerance for separation, fragile attachment, or still needs stable support.
1203.trigger: The client denies or strongly avoids the parting topic, shows obvious breakdown signs, or finds termination hard to bear due to chronic stress.

1204.skill_name: Checking change dimensions against general goals
1204.skill_description: Review symptoms, relationships, adaptation/defense flexibility, Reflection, Work and recreation, Independence one by one according to textual termination criteria, assessing the magnitude and stability of change; emphasizing that Symptom improvement alone is not enough for termination.
1204.when_to_use: When termination is preliminarily discussed or the termination stage begins, used to judge whether termination is mature and define follow-up consolidation focuses.
1204.trigger: The client says 'much better / want to end / how much longer can it continue', or enters termination discussion due to semester / project deadlines.

1205.skill_name: Guide comparison of concrete changes between 'now and before'
1205.skill_description: Point out specific differences from early stages, invite them to review new views and behaviors in the remaining weeks, prompting the client to self-report and name gains, to integrate and consolidate change.
1205.when_to_use: In the review and consolidation segment of the ending stage, used to organize scattered progress into a coherent change narrative.
1205.trigger: The client describes improvement in new reactions, new abilities, or relationships, sexual functioning, relaxation, etc., or spontaneously compares the past with the present.

1206.skill_name: Acknowledging what has not yet changed and disappointment, and clarifying the complete-cure Fantasy
1206.skill_description: Point out 'some changed, some not yet changed', explore Fantasies of complete cure and impossibility and their disappointment, using the 'good enough' frame to help accept abilities and limitations, calibrating Anticipations.
1206.when_to_use: When grief appears in the ending stage or regrets about imperfection, used to ground expectations and ease harsh demands for not yet being fully recovered.
1206.trigger: The client expresses disappointment, depression, brief return of old symptoms, or reveals Fantasies like 'should be completely cured/thoroughly different' in speech.

1207.skill_name: Summative feedback and setting pragmatic Anticipations and check-in options
1207.skill_description: Summarize emotional and functional improvements in a sincere tone, reminding that future pressure and old ways may return, expressing confidence and explaining that short-term check-ins are possible when needed, establishing pragmatic Anticipations.
1207.when_to_use: In the last few sessions and goodbye segments, used to share the therapist's views on change and future challenges and to close.
1207.trigger: Approaching the last one or two sessions, the client asks 'how do you see this treatment', or talks about future worries and whether they can return.

1208.skill_description: Check whether the client attributes the gains to themselves rather than the therapist, take internalized self-efficacy and independence as termination clues; if still markedly dependent, continue exploring and handling.
1208.when_to_use: Deciding whether to end and at the consolidation stage, used to judge the degree of internalization of change and readiness to leave.
1208.trigger: The client says 'I cannot do without you/you cured me' or conversely 'I want to try on my own', revealing strong dependence or autonomy wishes.

1186.skill_name: Prioritizing Reflection focus through the ending lens
1186.skill_description: At the ending stage use the principles of choice and preparation, examine the material with the 'ending lens'. By default, emotions, dreams, new relationships, and symptoms may be related to termination; think about their connection with loss and regression, and prioritize focusing on the closing themes to organize understanding.
1186.when_to_use: At the termination stage (planned or unilateral), aiming to wrap up and consolidate understanding; the client is cooperative but emotionally fluctuating, and the experience needs integration.
1186.trigger: During the termination period, the client frequently raises new topics, dreams, strong emotions, or a resurgence of old patterns, making the material appear scattered or contradictory.

1187.skill_description: Connect the dream's imagery with ambivalence about ending treatment, naming and organizing polar emotions like 'excitement about new possibilities' and 'Anxiety about being alone', helping the client understand the dream's mapping of the termination experience.
1187.when_to_use: At the termination stage, when the client reports dreams themed on separation, journeys, or setting sail, used to distill the dream's termination meaning.
1187.trigger: Departure/leaving/spaceflight/Being alone and other imagery appear in dreams, the client simultaneously showing excitement and unease or a hollow feeling.

1188.skill_name: Reflecting on the compensatory meaning of new relationships
1188.skill_description: Understand new relationships appearing or deepening near the end as compensatory tendencies for losing the therapist, discerning their connections with grief and attachment needs, while not negating the new relationships' own value and potential benefits.
1188.when_to_use: In the termination period, when the client talks about new friends, a partner, or social expansion, used to understand separation reactions and substitute connections.
1188.trigger: The client quickly invests in or strengthens a relationship when approaching goodbyes, emphasizing expressions like 'no longer lonely/someone to accompany me'.

1189.skill_name: Treat relapse of old patterns as regression and link to termination
1189.skill_description: Treat the reappearance of old symptoms, old transference, or early rule conflicts as predictable Regression in the termination phase, reflecting on their associations with separation and loss, avoiding misjudging as not yet ready to end.
1189.when_to_use: When lateness, re-disputes over bills/cancellation policies, or a resurgence of old symptoms are observed at the termination stage, their meaning and emotional source need to be clarified.
1189.trigger: The client is late again, nitpicks about fees, old Anxiety or doubts rekindle, or again questions the therapist's care and reliability.

1190.skill_name: Understand anger and disappointment as separation reactions or defenses
1190.skill_description: Reflect strong anger or disappointment toward the therapist as reactions to unfinished business, or as defenses masking grief and loss; organizing understanding within this frame to maintain the alliance and closing focus.
1190.when_to_use: During termination, when relationship tension rises and evaluations fluctuate, used to understand the separation themes and defensive functions behind emotions.
1190.trigger: The client accuses 'you are completely wrong/never so angry', or emphasizes contrasts with early stages, with strong and sharp emotions.

1191.skill_name: Connecting parting memories to distill ambivalent feelings
1191.skill_description: When the client recalls rituals or scenes with goodbye meanings, connect them with the parting experience of ending treatment, illuminating the ambivalent feeling of 'both expectant and sad' as the core Reflection theme.
1191.when_to_use: In the termination phase, when the client spontaneously talks about memories such as graduation, bonfire camp, farewell scenes, used to distill the emotional structure of separation.
1191.trigger: Narrations contain words like 'the last time/not seeing each other again', emotions showing joy and sorrow coexisting or nostalgia intertwined with moving forward.

1181.skill_name: Anticipating and identifying ending-phase Regression signals
1181.skill_description: Old symptoms and transference commonly resurge in the ending stage. Anticipate and identify Regression signs, such as being late again, re-raising bills/cancellation policies, jealousy toward others' sessions, treating them as phase characteristics rather than not being ready yet.
1181.when_to_use: In the planned or unilateral ending stage from the announced termination through the whole process, used to Listen to and frame the client's performance, avoiding misjudging treatment readiness due to Regression.
1181.trigger: The client after a long absence is late again, re-entangles fees/cancellation policy, or after the therapist is briefly distracted shows anger and jealousy, old symptom patterns suddenly return.

1182.skill_description: Identify the sadness and crying brought by parting, pointing out their origin in the real loss of losing the therapist; leaving room for emotions, helping the client see grief as a predictable, bearable, and worth-being-seen experience.
1182.when_to_use: In termination discussions and the last few weeks of sessions, when review and goodbyes become the core Work and grief appears or fluctuates.
1182.trigger: The client frequently sheds tears, repeatedly expressing 'very sad/reluctant to part', talking about worries that after ending, no one will listen and care like the therapist.

1183.skill_name: Assess end-phase depression and medication needs
1183.skill_description: Some individual clients become depressed in the ending stage. Assess depression severity and needs, discussing or coordinating medication when necessary, while maintaining a supportive stance, and explaining that these emotions sometimes resolve on their own.
1183.when_to_use: In the termination phase, when the grief intensifies to a point where self-relief is difficult, or the client proactively asks about medication and referral arrangements, used for safety and care decisions.
1183.trigger: In the termination period, the client self-reports being 'very depressed', with emotions hard to relieve, or directly proposes hoping to obtain medication treatment/psychiatric evaluation.

1184.skill_name: Identifying unspoken grief as possible resistance and inviting expression
1184.skill_description: If expressions of loss and grief never appear during the termination phase, treating it as a defense against painful emotions. Gently naming its possibility, inviting the client to describe feelings, thoughts, and associations about ending.
1184.when_to_use: In the last few sessions before termination, when farewell emotions that should normally appear are long absent, used to promote emotional expression and processing.
1184.trigger: The client insists on 'feeling nothing/nothing to say', avoiding any topics about ending, only talking about daily trivia or neutral content.

1185.skill_description: Explore Fantasies of being neglected, others 'taking up your time', and disappointment at the end of 'unlimited possibilities'; acknowledging emotions and limitations, helping the client understand the meaning of treatment and the relationship more realistically.
1185.when_to_use: When jealousy, anger, or complaints about the efficacy being 'not thorough enough' appear in the termination phase, used to link emotions to the processing of loss and expectations.
1185.trigger: After the therapist briefly answers a phone call, the client angrily says you care more about others, jealous that others 'take up her time'; or lamenting shyness/stress not yet fully gone and feeling disappointed.

1192.skill_name: Mark present-past differences and guide review
1192.skill_description: When the client shows reaction styles different from early stages, explicitly point out the 'now—past' differences, inviting them to jointly sort out the formation process and meaning in the coming sessions, to consolidate gains.
1192.when_to_use: The consolidation period of the ending stage; both sides have agreed the termination time is approaching, the alliance is stable, the goal is to take stock of key changes and turning points.
1192.trigger: The client narrates specific recent events, showing thinking or behaviors different from a year ago/early stages (e.g. more stable choices) and acknowledging 'I no longer think that way'.

1193.skill_name: Link new feelings with termination and limit new exploration
1193.skill_description: For a new feeling or image that suddenly emerges near the end, first briefly elicit associations to confirm its source; once it relates to termination, connect it back to the termination work, avoid opening up a new theme, and focus on closing and integration.
1193.when_to_use: In the weeks before termination; ending Work has unfolded, needing to prioritize termination-related emotions and Fantasies, avoiding scattered focus.
1193.trigger: The client suddenly brings up unfamiliar feelings/dreams or metaphors (e.g. 'like falling off a cliff') and mentions termination clues like 'not meeting again next week'.

1194.skill_name: Provide summarizing feedback in the final session
1194.skill_description: In the final or last few sessions, the therapist reviews the client's changes and functional improvement in a concise and clear way, realistically pointing out future challenges and possibly recurring old patterns, and explaining the option of check-ins, expressing a genuine goodbye.
1194.when_to_use: In the last one to several sessions; the client has shared what they gained, and both sides prepare to close in a structured way and integrate understanding.
1194.trigger: The client talks about change and its meaning multiple times in the last few weeks, or actively asks your views on the treatment and the future.

1195.skill_name: Moderately reduce neutrality to guide review and consolidation
1195.skill_description: In the alliance-stable termination phase, moderately relaxing neutrality, using guiding Questioning, brief labels, or moderate Humor to name familiar patterns, bringing material back to established themes to promote review and consolidation of gains.
1195.when_to_use: The ending stage; both sides have formed a 'tacit understanding' shared comprehension of the core pattern, needing to consolidate and summarize more directly.
1195.trigger: The client reproduces a theme or pattern already repeatedly discussed, and both parties are clear about its meaning and can reach consensus with brief prompts.

1196.skill_name: Frames change stability and relapse and provides review options
1196.skill_description: Realistically emphasizing that old ways may briefly return under future pressure, connecting their learned coping, proposing short-term follow-up visits when needed to 'get back on track', helping transfer gains to life outside treatment.
1196.when_to_use: The termination therapeutic review and transition planning stage; the goal is to stabilize change and set coping paths for rekindling.
1196.trigger: The client expresses worries about future pressure, anticipating old problems may reappear, or hoping for the possibility of further sessions when needed.

1175.skill_description: Directly ask the client why they want to end, listen carefully to their thoughts, emotions, and Fantasies about ending, discerning whether their wish is resistance or reasonable timing, and observing whether they can self-Interpretation and express ambivalence, using this to assess Reflection ability and readiness.
1175.when_to_use: When entering the ending stage or the client/therapist raises the ending topic, used to preliminarily assess whether the end is near and clarify motivation and readiness.
1175.trigger: The client actively proposes ending; demanding termination on grounds of time/money; wanting to end right after starting to explore painful themes or new relationships; expressing anger or contempt toward the therapist while denying ambivalent feelings.

1176.skill_name: Directed association and connecting material with ending
1176.skill_description: Invite the client to freely associate about recent emotions, dreams, and new relationships, and explicitly probe their association with ending, observing whether they can spontaneously connect and self-Interpretation (e.g. parting, Loneliness, compensation), to assess Reflection and pattern-identification ability.
1176.when_to_use: Having entered the ending stage, needing to prioritize the client's material through the 'ending lens' when identifying core emotions and themes.
1176.trigger: The client reports dreams related to parting/escaping; describing feelings of 'like falling off a cliff'; starting new relationships in the ending phase; recalling bonfires, goodbyes and other parting imagery.

1177.skill_name: Pointing out and exploring regression and grief
1177.skill_description: Identify common Regression and grief in the ending phase, normalizing them and encouraging expression of the sense of loss, observing whether the client can recognize recurring old patterns (e.g. jealousy, possessiveness) and process sadness rather than avoiding defensively, to assess self-awareness and emotional Reflection ability.
1177.when_to_use: When symptom/behavior recurrence or significant sadness appears in the ending phase, used to distinguish readiness from resistance and assess Reflection ability.
1177.trigger: The client is late again, questions fees/cancellation policy; cries or is depressed in the session; is intensely angry/jealous due to the therapist's occasional mistake.

1178.skill_name: Guiding review and naming of change
1178.skill_description: Moderately relaxing neutrality, naming specific functional/viewpoint changes and inviting review of their formation process, assessing whether the client can clearly name differences, interpreting change and consolidating gains, as indicators of their self-Interpretation and pattern-identification ability.
1178.when_to_use: At the closing and consolidation period of the ending stage, especially in recent weeks when treatment effects need systematic review.
1178.trigger: The client describes handling situations differently from before (e.g. different reactions to temptation/relationships); spontaneously noting 'I no longer think that way'.

1179.skill_name: Propose hypotheses linking transference and interpersonal patterns
1179.skill_description: Gently confront and clarify the connection between the wish to end and existing interpersonal expectations/transference, do transference interpretation where necessary, and observe whether the client can use the new understanding to adjust present choices (such as continuing to work), so as to test their ability to use insight under pressure.
1179.when_to_use: When the wish to terminate may be driven by resistance or old patterns, or familiar themes such as 'being controlled/stuck' appear.
1179.trigger: The client says 'stuck here' 'you will not let me leave'; unwilling to let the new partner know about treatment; claiming 'it is enough' while the therapist senses key issues are not yet completed.

1180.skill_name: Share therapeutic observations and assess integrative capacity
1180.skill_description: Sharing views on change, residual challenges, and future coping in the last few sessions, noticing the client's acceptance, digestion, and planning ability regarding grounded feedback, to assess their Reflection integration and self-regulation readiness.
1180.when_to_use: The last few sessions of a planned ending, used for closing, goodbyes, and testing internalization and self-maintenance ability.
1180.trigger: Approaching the final session; discussing goodbyes and the future; the client asking about post-ending arrangements or views on the treatment's meaning.

1236.skill_name: Arranges and implements post-termination phone follow-up and scale re-examination
1236.skill_description: At the ending, schedule follow-ups and at the agreed nodes conduct telephone follow-ups (such as one month or half a year later), learn about changes in symptom subsiding and life/study adaptation, conduct scale rechecks when necessary to track the maintenance and fluctuation of efficacy, give praise and support; if problems are found, promptly reassess or recommend a return visit, to consolidate and test the treatment effect.
1236.when_to_use: When formulating a follow-up support plan at the end of treatment/counseling, or from termination to the follow-up stage, when at the agreed follow-up points (such as one month or half a year later) maintenance needs to be consolidated and monitored.
1236.trigger: The treatment/counseling has ended and there is a need to know the follow-up situation; or the client is about to leave treatment, return to school/start an internship, enter an examination-preparation period, and reports the recent situation or has worries about maintaining the effect.

1231.skill_name: Assess self-explanation and acceptance and comment on the treatment method
1231.skill_description: Invite them to review the influence of growth experience and acceptance, encourage expressing views and reactions about the treatment methods and explain the techniques and mechanisms, observe emotional absorption and self-explanation ability; at the same time guide them to narrate in their own language their new understanding and acceptance of the self and record concrete examples, to judge whether reflective capacity has stably formed and how it is used in relationships and life.
1231.when_to_use: At the review and summary of the ending stage, or when resistance and doubt appear, used to assess and consolidate the stability of self-interpretation and acceptance.
1231.trigger: The client can describe connections between past experiences and the present, expressing 'more understanding, more acceptance'; or raising doubts about the treatment, finding the methods inappropriate, showing defensive reactions and emotional fluctuations.

1234.skill_name: Connecting past patterns with current behaviors to assess Reflection ability
1234.skill_description: Help them connect early experiences and Defense mechanisms with current Anxiety, somatization, and relationship patterns; invite them to describe present emotions and bodily experiences and contrast them with 'should/should not' beliefs; review special emotional experiences and key time clues to discern inner connections, assessing whether they can connect emotions and behaviors, Interpretation the sources of emotions, and revise rigid cognitions, as indicators of Reflection ability maturity.
1234.when_to_use: In the Consolidation and termination stage, when symptoms have lessened and inner patterns begin to be explored, needing to assess self-Interpretation and pattern-identification ability.
1234.trigger: The client can recall early experiences and discuss current distress; strong moralizing judgments or descriptions of emotional confusion appear; or narration of multiple experiences is messy, emotion sources unclear or disconnected from each other.

1215.skill_name: Invite the client to self-assess and summarize changes
1215.skill_description: Before the ending, invite the client to review in their own language the counseling course and key changes, mark the new-old differences combined with concrete life fragments, and optionally also summarize the improvements and the tension that still exists and the direction of later effort, promoting self-attribution, integration, and consolidation of the change.
1215.when_to_use: Termination and consolidation stage, the last one or two sessions, used to review and consolidate treatment effects and prepare for ending.
1215.trigger: Entering the closing stage; the client can self-reflect and list changes, or proactively mentions new realizations, gratitude, and a sense of growth.

1242.skill_name: The counselor assesses, feeds back, and names facilitating factors
1242.skill_description: The counselor, based on observation and materials (including written reflections), summarizes and feeds back concrete improvements, affirms the client's insights and changes with examples, reviews and names the elements that brought about change, and at the same time points out the focus for later self-help and continued effort, helping integrate and consolidate the gains.
1242.when_to_use: In the outcome-evaluation and summary segment of the ending stage, conducting a professional review and closing together with the client's self-evaluation.
1242.trigger: Stage-wise therapy has been completed with obvious improvement; the client asks about the reasons for change or needs to turn gains into self-help principles.

1237.skill_name: Jointly summarize counseling insights and concrete gains
1237.skill_description: Jointly review with the client the key insights and changes from the stage's counseling, link past problems with current improvement, distill sustainable strategies, and use concrete life changes as evidence marking the difference between old and new, consolidating gains for later autonomous application.
1237.when_to_use: In the ending review and consolidation stage, used to check effects and reach a closing consensus, or when the client proposes ending.
1237.trigger: Symptoms have improved and emotions are stable; or the client can summarize the changes in his own words, and improvements in functioning and relationships have been observed.

1224.skill_name: Review and integrate positive supportive resources
1224.skill_description: Lead the client to look back at warm memories and supportive resources awakened in counseling (relatives, friends, relationships, interests, etc.), summarizing how they reduced helplessness and Fear, and distilling sustainable ways of using resources, enhancing subsequent coping and reuse.
1224.when_to_use: Used in the ending stage to consolidate gains, reduce relapse risk, and prepare before returning to real life.
1224.trigger: The client is still dominated by negative narratives, ignoring moments of being loved or the support nearby.

1223.skill_name: Re-test before ending and feed back quantified change
1223.skill_description: Before the ending, re-test key scales (such as the AIS/SAS/SDS), compare with the initial test and jointly interpret the score changes, objectively mark the improvement in sleep, emotion, etc. and the degree of goal attainment, clarify the areas still needing effort, as evidence for the treatment review.
1223.when_to_use: Before and after the last session or near termination, used for efficacy evaluation, confirming goal achievement, and supporting closing decisions.
1223.trigger: First assessment data or retest results are available; near the end, efficacy needs evaluating, or the client is concerned about objective progress.

1232.skill_name: Integrate subjective, objective, and functional indicators to assess symptom improvement
1232.skill_description: In continuous sessions and return visits, jointly review with the client the changes in emotions and core symptoms, concretize 'improvement' into reproducible instances; simultaneously record self-rating proportions, mental appearance and functional indicators such as study/socializing, and mutually corroborate them with on-site observation or scale results, comprehensively judging the magnitude and stability of the improvement.
1232.when_to_use: In the mid-to-Consolidation and termination assessment stage, or in post-course follow-ups, used to summarize efficacy and judge whether termination is near.
1232.trigger: The client self-reports improvement or no longer only talks about symptoms; nonverbal changes showing increased vitality; exams/activities or family feedback showing functional improvement; reaching planned follow-up milestones.

1214.skill_name: Integrate multi-source evidence to review symptom and emotional improvement
1214.skill_description: Based on the client's self-report, check whether positive emotional experiences have increased and whether low mood can self-adjust; guide reviewing changes in insomnia, overthinking, Anxiety, interpersonal sensitivity with concrete facts, and connecting insights gained in counseling; comprehensively validating improvement and stability with client, counselor, and homeroom teacher/family feedback, providing the basis for ending and consolidation.
1214.when_to_use: At the consolidation-goal and evaluation stage or the review session before case closure; the comprehensive evaluation at the third consultation or before the end.
1214.trigger: The client states 'improved emotions' 'improved sleep/relationships' or considers ending; on-site observation of improved mental outlook and communication; multiple-source improvement clues appear or self-reports and others' reports are inconsistent and need verification.

1238.skill_name: Tracks session emotion and nonverbal indicators to confirm symptom relief
1238.skill_description: Compare emotional and behavioral indicators in sessions before and after treatment, such as crying frequency, speech rate and tone, ability to face the counselor directly, not shaking legs/squeezing hands, more relaxed expressions, smiling, actively discussing plans, and changes from deny to being able to verbalize pain, recording 'significantly reduced/more controllable', to evidence substantive improvement and stability of symptoms such as depression, Anxiety.
1238.when_to_use: At each follow-up and stage summary, in the final sessions or ending evaluation, when in-session improvement evidence needs to be made objective.
1238.trigger: It is observed that emotional reactions such as crying in sessions have clearly decreased compared with the early stage, and verbal and nonverbal expression is more relaxed and frank; the client proactively reports that suffering has lessened and discusses realistic plans; begins spontaneously expressing concrete feeling words.

1217.skill_name: Telephone follow-up to verify symptom stability and maintenance / recurrence
1217.skill_description: In the ending and follow-up stage, conduct agreed phone follow-ups, verifying whether Fear and Anxiety have disappeared or stabilized, collecting subjective feelings about emotional, cognitive, and behavioral changes; asking whether tension and communication adaptation when returning to school and meeting classmates and teachers are maintained, assessing whether recurrence appears, and judging whether further sessions are needed for support and plan adjustment.
1217.when_to_use: Before ending, set follow-up arrangements and follow-up points from short-term to medium- and long-term after ending (such as one month, several months); when session intervals are long and the between-session state needs to be tracked.
1217.trigger: The client has paused or ended the interviews, the chief complaint symptoms are reduced and need remote verification; the agreed follow-up time arrives or slight fluctuations appear.

1212.skill_name: Re-administer scales and compare to objectively assess symptom change
1212.skill_description: In stage reviews or follow-ups, retest Scales such as SAS, SDS, SCL-90, SIOSS, comparing with initial tests or norms, quantitatively judging the change magnitude of core indicators such as Anxiety, depression, suicide ideation and whether they have returned to normal ranges, using objective data to evidence subjective improvement and assess trends.
1212.when_to_use: In the effectiveness-assessment segment before Consolidation and termination, or when objective verification is needed during follow-up periods such as about a month after ending.
1212.trigger: Entering the review/summary or retest step, with before-and-after scores obtained; the client's reported improvement needs objective verification, or assessment results are obtained through participation in a mental health survey.

1254.skill_name: Explain and confirm the return-visit and re-appointment channel
1254.skill_description: At the end, clearly inform that they can contact the counselor promptly when encountering difficulties later, explaining the channel and conditions of 'can come to the counseling center for appointments when needed', and confirming and accepting the client's willingness of 'willing to come again if needed', providing realistic, accessible support to reduce worries and separation discomfort, supporting the transition without reinforcing dependence.
1254.when_to_use: When the ending decision is reached at the last or penultimate session, used to explain the follow-up contact and support channels and accept the willingness for return visits.
1254.trigger: When ending is near and the client worries about future difficulties or raises the idea of possibly needing help in the future, or explicitly expresses willingness to seek help or follow up again.

1245.skill_name: Affirm growth and give life advice and best wishes
1245.skill_description: In the final session, truthfully point out the positive changes observed, expressing delight and support, giving specific wishes (e.g. success in postgraduate exams), and summarizing and giving life-oriented advice before ending, such as going with the flow, lowering expectations, cultivating interests, participating in group activities, communicating more, improving social skills, to consolidate improvement, supporting goodbyes and returning to daily life.
1245.when_to_use: In the ending-stage goodbye session or the final session, used to consolidate strategies and support transitioning to the future, returning to daily life.
1245.trigger: The client expresses gratitude, shows stable improvement, and is about to end counseling, or is about to return to daily life and needs concrete, executable maintenance and adaptation strategies.

1220.skill_name: Raises and clarifies termination, confirms readiness and negotiates arrangements
1220.skill_description: When observing symptoms gradually fading and counseling entering its final stage, actively discuss the achievement of counseling goals and the Anticipated end time, propose ending suggestions and jointly confirm with the client their readiness and willingness to cope independently; the counselor explains using loosened defenses and core beliefs and external interpersonal changes as the basis, negotiating arrangements and specific closing matters for ending preparation, and reaching an ending consensus when the client is reluctant to part.
1220.when_to_use: Symptoms have improved stably, counseling is entering the ending stage or it is the last session, used to plan the termination process, confirm readiness, and negotiate concrete arrangements.
1220.trigger: The client reduces Anxiety narration, is stable, and says 'not so anxious lately', showing stable improvements in behavior, relationships, and self-expression, both sides indicating they can face life alone; or entering the final session to begin discussing ending and arrangements.

1240.skill_name: Discuss ending feelings in the here and now and clarify differences
1240.skill_description: Invite the client here and now to express complex emotions about ending and the counselor (dissatisfaction, attachment, excitement, etc.), accepting and clarifying differences, listening to their attitudes and concerns, facilitating a shared understanding of ending, reducing the burden of the unspoken, supporting a smooth closing.
1240.when_to_use: Near the final session or when present emotions related to ending appear, used to explore and organize feelings about ending.
1240.trigger: The client mentions ending feelings, showing Silence or emotional fluctuations, or expresses views and dissatisfaction about the counselor.

1248.skill_name: Asking about and assessing recovery of daily, study, and work social functioning
1248.skill_description: Through open inquiry, record recently begun daily activities, study arrangements, social participation, and work performance, using concrete functions such as walking, shopping, study plans, independent business trips, and being praised as references, to assess the improvement and stability of adaptation and role functioning.
1248.when_to_use: In the initial evaluation and consolidation stages, and at the comprehensive review before the end or the follow-up stage, used to judge functional improvement.
1248.trigger: The client reports new or resumed daily, study, or work activities and plans; or when the sources of improvement or difficulty in study, interpersonal, and daily activities need to be judged.

1250.skill_name: Reviews and affirms self-management success to consolidate functional improvement
1250.skill_description: Guide the client to recall the sleep and mood improvements obtained through self-management, discuss the positive impacts on study, physical strength, and socializing, and give timely affirmation to consolidate the functional improvement.
1250.when_to_use: In the consolidation stage, summarizing progress, enhancing confidence, and assessing functional improvement.
1250.trigger: The client reports successful experiences or peers evaluate one's improvement; functional changes need to be consolidated.

1221.skill_name: Assessing self-awareness and reality testing with real problems and ideal narratives
1221.skill_description: Select specific tasks and events in Learning, relationships, and family to review, analyzing self-feelings, behaviors, and others' reactions, distinguishing facts from Interpretations, and combining expressions about future ideals, self-abilities, relationships, and Safety, comprehensively assessing self-positioning, self-awareness, and reality-testing levels.
1221.when_to_use: In the 7th–8th Consolidation and termination stage, or when needing to understand self-awareness, value orientation, and reality-testing levels.
1221.trigger: The client faces concrete tasks or real predicaments needing assessment of coping ability; discussing family interaction and self-evaluation; confused about the future or able to describe personal ideals and relationship orientations.

1247.skill_name: Explore self-trust and active investigation to disconfirm
1247.skill_description: Around concrete behavioral details, explore the degree of self-trust (such as repeatedly confirming even habituated behaviors), and assess whether they can proactively verify and revise beliefs through investigation; at the same time examine whether their realistic cognition of their own mental health has shifted from doubt toward a more consistent explanation, to reflect the improvement of reality-testing ability.
1247.when_to_use: When wrong beliefs have been identified and need validation and reinforcement of mature cognition, in stages and reviews; assessing the stability of self-awareness and realistic cognition in the consolidation phase.
1247.trigger: The client is willing to try or has conducted investigations; still insists others can see through their thoughts and this needs disproving; still highly doubts completed routine behaviors and repeatedly checks; expresses a re-judgment of their own mental health or corrects previous erroneous cognition.

1225.skill_name: Identifying and feeding back changes in defense patterns and adaptive shifts
1225.skill_description: In reviewing recent interpersonal fragments, identify defense patterns (e.g. Emotional isolation, Intellectualization, Reaction formation) and shifts from non-adaptive defenses such as devaluation toward more adaptive approaches and perspective-taking understanding, and give feedback, assessing improvements in emotional contact and self-regulation, as indicators of improved Ego functions.
1225.when_to_use: In the mid-to-consolidation assessment stage, when reviewing interaction fragments or when the client can start talking about feelings but still avoids with Intellectualization.
1225.trigger: Narrating as if talking about someone else's affairs, talking endlessly while avoiding emotions, or gradually able to freely explore feelings; showing clues of understanding others, reduced devaluation, or less falling into interpersonal conflicts.

1230.skill_name: Reviewing and labeling defenses and changes in emotional expression to assess flexibility
1230.skill_description: Systematically sort out the journey from resistance, hidden aggression to being able to express and have aggressive emotions accepted, discussing past and current defense styles and their rightness or wrongness, and identifying and marking commonly used defenses (e.g. Undoing, omnipotent control, Emotional isolation, Regression) in session material, recording their occurrence situations and changes, to assess whether defenses are more flexible and adaptiveness improved.
1230.when_to_use: In the summary and evaluation sessions of late treatment; at the follow-up consolidation evaluation of sessions 13-14 or the systematic sorting before case closing.
1230.trigger: The client being able to review early resistance and attack experiences, express emotions fairly stably in the session, or mention trauma repair; being able to recall and describe past and current defensive reactions; reactions such as seeking verification, emotional detachment, or regressive dependence repeatedly appearing in the session.

1239.skill_name: Reviewing the course and integrating takeaways and evaluations
1239.skill_description: In the ending stage, systematically review the entire counseling course, symptom and functional changes, key insights and relationship experiences, inviting the client to self-report and self-rate satisfaction and residual distress with specific indicators of life and intimate relationships, objectively evaluating effectiveness and boundaries, clarifying main psychological causes and key Intervention points, pointing out directions still needing effort, integrating experiences to consolidate efficacy and prepare for goodbyes and subsequent arrangements.
1239.when_to_use: In the consecutive or final sessions of the ending stage, at the review and summary segment near termination, or when wrapping up the last session.
1239.trigger: Treatment approaches termination or enters the scheduled ending segment; the client is willing to talk about the treatment process and changes, reports improvement or still has remaining distress; the case or the counselor raises concern about the results of this round and whether to continue.

1219.skill_name: Proactively initiate termination discussion and time negotiation
1219.skill_description: After observing symptoms and distress gradually decreasing, promptly propose reviewing goal achievement, and jointly agree with the client on the Anticipated end time and pace, reserving sufficient and predictable preparation room for the closing stage.
1219.when_to_use: Used when counseling enters the later stage, the client's state tends to stabilize, and signs of change appear, to start planned closing and psychological preparation.
1219.trigger: The client self-reports reduced Anxiety recently, holds an open attitude toward ending, or Anxiety narration in counseling has clearly decreased.

1243.skill_name: Conveying trust and encouraging autonomous continuation
1243.skill_description: At the termination stage, convey trust in the client's self-regulation and recovery abilities, encourage them to solve problems with their own strength, continue self-awareness and exploration exercises, reduce dependence on treatment, and enhance self-esteem, supporting the independent continuation of change.
1243.when_to_use: When summarizing before ending and arranging the future, or in the closing and goodbye stage of the termination session, used to enhance autonomy and confidence.
1243.trigger: Discussing whether to rely on themselves to continue; the client worries about leaving support or shows obvious dependence; or expresses hope to continue treatment, feeling uncertain about future coping though symptoms have eased.

1252.skill_name: Share, witness, and give affirming responses
1252.skill_description: In the ending and consolidation stage, the counselor and client jointly review and share feelings about the counseling process, allowing and supporting one session themed on witnessing change/family session, presenting important others and growth achievements, expressing gratitude and commitment; when receiving letters after ending, replying in writing with sincere affirmation and connecting core themes in treatment, consolidating change and self-strength with moderate recognition, promoting smooth goodbyes.
1252.when_to_use: Around termination or in the closing stage with a stable relationship; when the set number of counseling sessions is completed and entering the ending and consolidation stage closing; or when receiving the client's letters and messages after ending.
1252.trigger: The client has subjective feelings about the counseling course needing expression; proposing to let the therapist meet their partner/children, expressing thanks or 'let me show you my changes'; or writing after ending to report grades, seeking confirmation and witnessing of change.

1241.skill_name: Conduct a structured summary of the consolidation phase
1241.skill_description: In the consolidation stage, review and briefly summarize the past counseling, set aside a clear period of time and a safe space, invite the client to in their own words systematically review the concrete changes, understanding and gains this stage brought, distill the key changes and insights and connect to the next arrangements, with a structured summary consolidate the outcomes, undertaking the ending closure.
1241.when_to_use: Used at the last two sessions when approaching ending treatment or entering the consolidation stage, or at sessions near the end for closing and integration.
1241.trigger: At the end of the session, staged goal completion appears; the client asks about subsequent arrangements or feels lost about the changes and needs sorting out; or in the closing session begins to review and is willing to summarize what was gained in this stage.

1244.skill_name: Provide summative feedback and schedule follow-up re-testing
1244.skill_description: Give concise, clear professional feedback at termination, summarizing change and goal achievement, and agreeing on or implementing subsequent follow-up/tracking; in the final or penultimate session, compare initial and final assessments and life performance (e.g. suicide ideation Scale scores, activity participation, parent-child interaction), combining subjective feelings, concretely presenting change trajectories, helping the client internalize achievements and assess maintenance effects.
1244.when_to_use: At the very end of the ending stage and shortly after it ends, or when reviewing outcomes and consolidating change in the last/penultimate session.
1244.trigger: When after completing the staged assessment there is a need to consolidate the change and monitor the maintenance effect; there are comparable data from the first and last measurements; the client shows changes in life participation, parent-child interaction or subjective state.

1226.skill_name: Guide quantified self-assessment and integrate evidence to summarize change
1226.skill_description: In the termination or stage review, invite the client to self-assess the changes by concrete life domains and situations, combined with scoring and subjective narration; simultaneously verify with symptom and function indicators, the three lines of emotion-speech-behavior, and multi-source feedback from counselors/classmates, record and concretize the results, affirm the progress, forming a realistic and internalized change assessment.
1226.when_to_use: Near the end or at a stage review segment, needing to summarize outcomes, integrate subjective and objective evidence, and consolidate self-efficacy.
1226.trigger: The client proactively states recent updates, begins to summarize gains, or reports symptom/function improvement; or needs others' observation to corroborate subjective improvement.

1216.skill_name: Review the course of treatment and provide realistic feedback and direction
1216.skill_description: Jointly review with the client the counseling course and the changes that have occurred, based on the material and goals give professional and restrained realistic feedback, avoid exaggerating or promising complete recovery; concretely point out the aspects still needing continued effort, when needed use recent concrete events to contrast functional changes, helping to clarify the subsequent self-improvement direction.
1216.when_to_use: In the middle of the 5th counseling session or at the summary stage before the end, or at the termination session / outcome evaluation, used to prepare for the wrap-up and clarify the subsequent direction.
1216.trigger: The client presents improvement and is about to end, proactively seeks a summary or asks about next steps; the counseling process has formed continuous observation and goal-achievement evidence.

1227.skill_name: Invite self-rated efficacy and jointly decide on termination
1227.skill_description: Invite the client to self-evaluate the efficacy in their own language and with life feedback, record positive changes and residual problems; combined with concrete reports of symptom and functioning improvement, jointly agree on the ending time point; if they question the effect, recent concrete situations can be compared with early reactions to examine the real change.
1227.when_to_use: At the ending stage and effect-evaluation segment, when the patient reports obvious improvement or finds it hard in reality to continue frequent visits, and whether to end needs joint evaluation.
1227.trigger: The patient expresses satisfaction with treatment and reports family/Symptom improvement, or actively describes experiences like 'much more confident'; may also propose 'feeling no effects'.

1235.skill_name: Review the journey and consolidate cognitive and change gains
1235.skill_description: Before ending, review the entire counseling course, summarizing gains and difficulties, comparing specific pre/post manifestations in cognition, emotion, and behavior, giving specific affirmation and encouragement, while truthfully pointing out remaining insufficiencies, consolidating cognitive change and self-awareness formed in treatment, helping integrate experience and stabilize improvement.
1235.when_to_use: At the ending and consolidation stage of the last session of the term or treatment, used for overall review and forming a realistic conclusion about change.
1235.trigger: As treatment nears its end, the client's symptoms are markedly reduced and they are willing to review; or expectations about later challenges and 'full recovery' need calibration.

1218.skill_name: Truthfully presenting improved and not-yet-improved aspects and calibrating Anticipations
1218.skill_description: In efficacy reviews, specifically listing improved and not-yet-improved aspects, probing causes (e.g. dissatisfaction with teachers, resistance and avoidance), first affirming progress then directly stating the incompleteness of change and residual worries, summarizing functional changes in a realistic tone, preventing the 'complete cure' Fantasy and establishing pragmatic Anticipations and follow-up concerns.
1218.when_to_use: In the mid-to-late treatment or termination summary of change, used to truly assess 'what changed and what has not yet changed' and calibrate expectations.
1218.trigger: The scales indicate mild symptoms remain; the client reports partial improvement while still having distress, or expresses worry that 'it is still one or two points short'.

1213.skill_name: Re-administer and compare scales to objectively present change
1213.skill_description: In the ending stage, retest scales such as the SAS, SDS, SIOSS, SES, AIS, record the standard scores and compare longitudinally with the initial assessment, observe whether they have returned to the normal range, quantifying the degree of change in sleep and emotions; with concrete data, objectively present the efficacy, verify progress, calibrate subjective impressions and consolidate confidence in the change.
1213.when_to_use: In the outcome-evaluation stage at the end of a phase or before termination, used to quantitatively verify the counseling effect and summarize the therapeutic effect.
1213.trigger: Multiple sessions have been completed and initial assessment scales exist, and end-stage measurement data are obtained; or the client needs objective evidence to confirm improvement.

1253.skill_name: Rehearsing and assessing self Emotion management and independent behavior
1253.skill_description: Rehearse the 'awareness—naming—connection—self-talk' self-regulation process with the client, asking whether situations that previously needed companionship can now be completed alone, and assessing their independent application ability without the counselor's support; also agreeing on help-seeking channels when encountering obstacles.
1253.when_to_use: At the consolidation and closing stage before termination or the follow-up stage, used to assess the ability to maintain improvement independently.
1253.trigger: The client worries about relapse or has a history of Emotional loss of control; previously avoided Being alone or solo-travel scenes and self-reports change after treatment.

1251.skill_name: Inquires into change attribution and assesses self-efficacy and agency
1251.skill_description: Ask about the main attribution of progress (own efforts or external support), record spontaneous actions outside sessions and self-attributions, assessing their confidence and specific plans for continued improvement, to judge whether dependence has decreased and maintenance is possible without ongoing support.
1251.when_to_use: Before termination or when entering the consolidation period, to assess independence and the ability to maintain improvements.
1251.trigger: The client expresses that they can adjust on their own and is very confident, or reports autonomous behavior and describes their own role and responsibility in the improvement.

1249.skill_name: Assess maintenance and expansion capacity after support is withdrawn
1249.skill_description: Through the final session and subsequent follow-ups, verifying whether change can be maintained and expanded without ongoing support, e.g. autonomous attempts between sessions making progress or independently making related decisions outside treatment, as indicators of Independence.
1249.when_to_use: When preparing to end and at short-term follow-up after ending or between-session assessment, used to confirm the ability to independently maintain and expand.
1249.trigger: Planning to go out to study/work; practicing autonomously and successfully between the two meetings; or reporting that they have already made treatment-related decisions on their own.

1233.skill_name: Explores termination preparation and self-help plans and assesses attachment changes
1233.skill_description: In goodbyes and separation processing, directly asking how they will use their own strength to maintain change after ending, combining early Safety needs and later discussed and agreed changes to end, recording autonomy expressions, to assess reduced dependence and the feasibility of independent Work.
1233.when_to_use: Discuss ending and follow-up arrangements in the closing stage
1233.trigger: Able to discuss and accept the ending arrangements, expresses hope to continue treatment while also solving problems with their own strength, and the need for retention and shelter within the session weakens.

1229.skill_name: Before termination, formulate self-maintenance strategies and ending criteria
1229.skill_description: Before ending, make clear that 'improvement takes a process', discuss self-help maintenance strategies after termination (such as continued practice, sleep habits), and possibly set conditional open-ended termination criteria, assessing execution confidence and feasible arrangements to judge independence.
1229.when_to_use: The last counseling session or a session near the end, used to plan post-termination maintenance.
1229.trigger: Symptoms have markedly improved; the client states 'I am very confident' and asks whether treatment can end or hopes to self-regulate.

1228.skill_name: Record autonomy indicators to assess reduced dependence
1228.skill_description: Treat the client's actively proposing termination and negotiating the ending with the counselor, actively participating in group activities during follow-up, and the contrast between previously passive endings and this active choice, as evidence of autonomous decision-making and reduced dependence, to be included in the independence assessment.
1228.when_to_use: At the ending stage and in follow-up, reviews relationship changes and assesses whether independent maintenance ability is present.
1228.trigger: The client actively proposes termination or spontaneously compares past relationships with this counseling experience; follow-ups need assessing whether they still depend on urging.

1222.skill_name: Verifying self-maintenance and Emotion management without ongoing support
1222.skill_description: Ask about and verify whether in daily life and at follow-up they can independently use the mastered emotion-handling methods, or adopt alternative self-regulation strategies in non-treatment situations, and observe whether the improvement in emotion and behavior continues stably after an interval, so as to judge that dependence has decreased.
1222.when_to_use: In the Consolidation and termination stage, stage or post-termination follow-ups, used to test independent maintenance ability.
1222.trigger: Recent stress or emotional fluctuations with feedback on self-regulation practice; reporting stable scores or independent coping after consultation intervals; not yet increasing help-seeking after stressful events and actively using constructive strategies.

1246.skill_name: Explore change attribution and internalization of self-help strategies
1246.skill_description: Inquire whether change mainly originates from their own practice and insight, such as self-analysis and self-soothing, or from their own choices; and clarify the attribution and degree of dependence on the treatment and self-effort, to assess the internalization and autonomy of the improvement.
1246.when_to_use: When approaching the end or formulating an ending plan, at consolidation assessment dialogues, reviewing growth and summarizing treatment effects.
1246.trigger: The client actively talks about self-analysis or self-comfort experiences; saying 'I am better' and interpreting past behaviors and defenses; finding the treatment ineffective or emphasizing that willpower alone can control; or appearing in gratitude contexts with expressions like 'who changed me'.
